title: Quentin and the Hollow
premise: Ulyana Zhou, a memory-thief hiding in the magic-outlawed city of Vessing, has spent twelve years selling stolen recollections as harmless charms. When a mute child arrives speaking a pre-kingdom tongue that only Ulyana can half-understand through her stolen memories, she learns the child is a living key to the Hollow—a country erased from maps and minds alike—and that its erasure is spreading to devour anyone who remembers it. Hunted by the Ministry of Forgetting and shadowed by her old partner turned inquisitor, Ulyana must gather the scattered memories of the Hollow from the people she once robbed, including the one memory she swore never to sell: her own first love, who died there. In the end, Ulyana finds the door out of the Hollow only by giving up every memory of the person she loved most, choosing the child's survival over her own past—and waking on the far side of the door whole, free, and unable to remember why she is crying.
about_author: Lior Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing letters no one ever claimed, an experience that left a lasting fascination with what people choose to remember. They write quiet, aching fantasy about ordinary people caught in the machinery of history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A day in her carefully small life: lifting a widow's memory of her wedding, selling it back as a charm, keeping her head down in Vessing where magic means the gallows. The beat is controlled loneliness—she has made invisibility an art and calls it safety.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Hour of Ash
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the night the Ministry burns a suspected witch two streets over, a child appears at her door, barefoot, silent, speaking a language that makes Ulyana's stolen memories stir unbidden. The beat is dread wrapped in tenderness: she knows better than to open doors, and opens it anyway.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The child's speech matches fragments in memories Ulyana stole years ago—from a dying smuggler, from a mad priest. She realizes the language belongs to the Hollow, a country officially proven never to have existed. The beat is vertigo: her inventory of stolen lives is suddenly a map.

chapters.title: What the Ministry Burns
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with a cold interlude from Inquisitor Dain Marrow's ledger. The Ministry notices anomalies: charms circulating with impossible provenance, a child-shaped absence in the census. Ulyana hides the boy, Tam, in her cellar. The beat is paranoia tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: The Partner Who Forgot Me
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Dain Marrow comes to her shop—not arresting, but asking questions too gently. Twelve years ago he was her partner in theft and something more; now his memories of her have been professionally edited. The beat is grief disguised as small talk, love against duty established on both sides.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She sorts her charm-stock for Hollow fragments and finds a pattern: everyone who remembered the Hollow has died or forgotten within a year. Tam draws a door in the dust—the same door from the smuggler's memory. The beat is grim resolve: find the door before the forgetting finds them.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Sold Her Wedding Twice
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She tracks down a client whose purchased memory contained a true fragment of the Hollow, but the woman has already been visited by Ministry 'archivists.' Ulyana escapes with the fragment and a name: the Cartographer, who maps places that no longer exist. The beat is guilt—her trade has left a trail of casualties.

chapters.title: Streets That Remember Being Rivers
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tam's POV alternating. Following Tam's instincts through Vessing's oldest quarter, they find places where the city's shape disagrees with itself—staircases to nowhere, a canal under the cobbles. Tam speaks more each day; the Hollow is leaking into him. The beat is wonder curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Cartographer, an exiled scholar named Ivo Renk, agrees to help because Ulyana once stole a memory he needed and never sold it. He reveals the Hollow wasn't destroyed—it was traded away in a treaty, its existence used as currency. The beat is fury at the machinery of nations.

chapters.title: Duty Wears a Kind Face
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Ordered to investigate the memory-thief of Lowmarket, Dain reconstructs his own gaps and begins to suspect the woman he's hunting is someone he once loved. He falsifies his first report. The beat is a man cracking open between the duty that defines him and a feeling he can't source.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. To buy passage to the border ruins, she must sell a large, true memory—and chooses one of her own: a morning with Dain, twelve years ago. Selling it hurts less than expected, which frightens her more than the sale. The beat is the theme made flesh: survival always costs something you can't get back.

chapters.title: Border of the Unwritten
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tam's POV. At the border ruins they find the treaty-stone where the Hollow was signed away, and Tam touches it—and the stone remembers him. Ministry riders appear; Ivo holds them off and is taken. The beat is sacrifice and flight, the net closing.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Map
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV in custody, intercut with Ulyana's flight. Under questioning, Ivo gives the Ministry nothing but geography riddles while Ulyana and Tam cross the salt flats toward where the Hollow's door should stand. The beat is endurance—two kinds of courage, one behind bars, one running.

chapters.title: The Door That Was a Promise
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They find the door: not wood or stone but a standing agreement, held open by the accumulated memories of everyone who ever loved the Hollow. It will admit only those who carry a true memory of the country. Tam carries thousands. Ulyana carries almost none. The beat is despair at the threshold.

chapters.title: Everything I Stole, Everything I Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ransacking herself, she finds one buried true memory: her mother sang a lullaby from the Hollow; Ulyana's thieving career began by stealing her own childhood back from a buyer. The door recognizes her. The beat is revelation—she was always from the Hollow; exile was the theft.

chapters.title: Inside the Erased
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, dreamlike. Within the Hollow: a country mid-erasure, streets going grey at the edges, its last inhabitants living on borrowed recollection. Tam is welcomed as the key that can re-anchor it—but anchoring requires a life freely given. The beat is terrible hospitality, love offered as a trap.

chapters.title: The Hollow's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Hollow's remnant council offers a choice: Tam stays and becomes the new anchor, or Ulyana surrenders all her memories of the person she loved most to feed the door. She realizes the memories they mean are of Dain—even the ones she sold have echoes here. The beat is the book's moral crux, stated plainly and cruelly.

chapters.title: What Dain Chose
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Having pieced together the truth, Dain deserts the Ministry, steals the treaty-ledger proving the Hollow's erasure was illegal, and rides for the salt flats—pursued by his own former colleagues. The beat is duty inverted: he finally obeys the self he can't remember being.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. As Ministry forces breach the Hollow's thinning borders, Ulyana pays the price: she feeds her love for Dain into the door, memory by memory, keeping only enough of herself to carry Tam through. Dain arrives at the threshold just as it closes—he sees her, and she no longer sees him. The beat is the climax: love against duty, duty winning, love paying anyway.

chapters.title: After the Forgetting
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the far side, in a country that does exist, Ulyana wakes with Tam, safe, employed papers forged by Ivo (released in the chaos), and an inexplicable ache. She cries at strangers' weddings without knowing why. The beat is hollow peace—the price paid, the survivor unaware of the bill.

chapters.title: The Man Who Bought Back Nothing
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Stripped of rank, Dain keeps the treaty-ledger and visits Ulyana's new shop under a pretext, buying a charm he doesn't need. She is polite to him as a stranger. He leaves the ledger with her anyway. The beat is quiet devastation: some debts survive even when the memory of them doesn't.

chapters.title: A Lullaby in an Unknown Tongue
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, closing. Tam hums the Hollow's lullaby; Ulyana finds herself harmonizing in a language she doesn't know she knows. In her stock of unsold charms she discovers one labeled in her own handwriting: do not sell. Inside it, faintly, a morning twelve years ago. The beat is bittersweet hope—memory outlasts its theft, and love, once given, is never entirely gone.
